exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
Bernoulli's equation for steady, incompressible, non-viscous streamline flow along a horizontal streamline ($y_1 = y_2$) states:
$$P + \frac{1}{2}\rho v^2 = \text{constant}$$
By the equation of continuity ($A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$), when the pipe cross-sectional area narrows, fluid flow velocity increases ($v_2 > v_1$), which causes dynamic pressure ($\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2$) to increase. Conservation of total mechanical energy dictates that static fluid pressure $P$ must decrease correspondingly.

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: A hydraulic lift has an input piston of radius $2\text{ cm}$ and an out put load piston of radius $20\text{ cm}$. What input force $F_1$ must be applied to lift an automobile of mass $1000\text{ kg}$? (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
According to Pascal's Principle, pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions:
$$P_1 = P_2 \implies \frac{F_1}{A_1} = \frac{F_2}{A_2} \implies F_1 = F_2 \left(\frac{A_1}{A_2}\right) = F_2 \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2$$
The load weight is $F_2 = mg = 1000\text{ kg} \times 10\text{ m/s}^2 = 10,000\text{ N}$.
$$F_1 = 10,000\text{ N} \times \left(\frac{2\text{ cm}}{20\text{ cm}}\right)^2 = 10,000 \times \left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^2 = 10,000 \times \frac{1}{100} = 100\text{ N}$$.

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: A steel rail of length $20\text{ m}$ is laid at an ambient temperature of $15^\circ\text{C}$. If the coefficient of linear expansion for steel is $\alpha = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$, how much will the rail expand when the temperature reaches $45^\circ\text{C}$?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
Thermal linear expansion is governed by:
$$\Delta L = L_0 \alpha \Delta T$$
Given $L_0 = 20\text{ m}$, $\alpha = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$, and $\Delta T = 45^\circ\text{C} - 15^\circ\text{C} = 30^\circ\text{C}$:
$$\Delta L = 20\text{ m} \times (1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}) \times 30^\circ\text{C} = 720 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 7.2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 7.2\text{ mm}$$.

If the coefficient of linear expansion for steel is $\alpha = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\ ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$, how much will the rail expand when the temperature reaches $45^\circ\text{C}$?

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: How much heat energy is required to raise the temperature of $2\text{ kg}$ of water from $20^\circ\text{C}$ to $70^\circ\text{C}$? (Specific heat capacity of water $c = 4200\text{ J}/(\text{kg}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$)
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
The quantity of heat absorbed is calculated using:
$$Q = m c \Delta T$$
Given $m = 2\text{ kg}$, $c = 4200\text{ J}/(\text{kg}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$, and $\Delta T = 70^\circ\text{C} - 20^\circ\text{C} = 50^\circ\text{C}$:
$$Q = 2\text{ kg} \times 4200\text{ J}/(\text{kg}\cdot^\circ\text{C}) \times 50^\circ\text{C} = 420,000\text{ J} = 420\text{ kJ}$$.

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: Two long, straight parallel wires separated by a distance $d$ carry currents $I_1$ and $I_2$ in the same direction. The nature and origin of the force between them is
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_d: zero because net charge is zero.
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
According to Ampere's force law and Biot-Savart law:
1. Wire 1 carrying current $I_1$ establishes a magnetic field at wire 2 directed perpendicular to wire 2 according to the right-hand grip rule.
2. By the Lorentz magnetic force rule ($\vec{F} = I_2 \vec{L} \times \vec{B}_1$), current $I_2$ flowing parallel to $I_1$ experiences an attractive magnetic force toward wire 1.
3. By Newton's third law, wire 1 experiences an equal and opposite attractive force toward wire 2. Thus, parallel currents in the same direction attract each other magnetically.

options: zero because net charge is zero.

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: In an AC circuit containing only a pure inductor of inductance $L$, the alternating voltage $V (t)$
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_a: is in phase with the alternating current $I (t)$.
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_b: leads the alternating current $I (t)$ by a phase angle of $90^\circ$ ($\pi/2\text{ rad}$).
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_c: lags behind the alternating current $I (t)$ by a phase angle of $90^\circ$ ($\pi/2\text{ rad}$).
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation: In a purely inductive AC circuit, self-inductance opposes changes in current through back emf ($v_L = L \frac{di}{dt}$). If current is $i (t) = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$, the voltage across the inductor is $v (t) = V_0 \cos(\omega t) = V_0 \sin(\omega t + \pi/2)$. Thus, the voltage leads the current by a phase angle of $90^\circ$ ($\pi/2\text{ rad}$), often remembered by the mnemonic 'ELI the ICE man'.

options: is in phase with the alternating current $I (t)$.
leads the alternating current $I (t)$ by a phase angle of $90^\circ$ ($\pi/2\text{ rad}$).
lags behind the alternating current $I (t)$ by a phase angle of $90^\circ$ ($\pi/2\text{ rad}$).

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: An AC series RLC circuit has resistance $R = 30\ \Omega$, inductive reactance $X_L = 80\ \Omega$, and cap a citive reactance $X_C = 40\ \Omega$. What is the total impedance $Z$ of the circuit?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
The impedance $Z$ of a series RLC circuit is:
$$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$$
Substituting the given values:
$$Z = \sqrt{30^2 + (80 - 40)^2} = \sqrt{30^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{900 + 1600} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\ \Omega$$.
exam-entrance-2016-phys.text: An AC series RLC circuit has resistance $R = 30\ \Omega$, inductive reactance $X_L = 80\ \Omega$, and cap a citive reactance $X_C = 40\ \Omega$. What is the total impedance $Z$ of the circuit?

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: What condition must be satisfied for resonance to occur in a series RLC AC circuit?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation: Resonance in an RLC series circuit occurs when the inductive reactance equals the cap a citive reactance ($X_L = X_C$, i.e., $\omega L = \frac{1}{\omega C}$). At this resonant frequency ($\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$), the net reactive impedance cancels to zero, leaving total impedance at its minimum value equal to resistance ($Z = R$), which causes the circuit current to reach its maximum amplitude.

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency and shortest wave length in the electromagnetic spectrum?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
In the electromagnetic spectrum arranged in order of increasing frequency and decreasing wave length:
Radio waves < Microwaves < Infrared < Visible Light < Ultraviolet < X-rays < Gamma rays. Gamma rays ($\gamma$-rays) have the highest frequencies ($> 10^{19}\text{ Hz}$) and shortest wave lengths ($< 10^{-11}\text{ m}$), carrying the highest photon energies ($E = hf$).

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: A stationary sound source emits sound of frequency $f$. If an observer moves away from the source with speed $v_o$, what happens to the perceived pitch and why?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_a: Higher pitch because waves arrive more frequently
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_b: Lower pitch because the relative speed of sound waves is reduced
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_c: Unchanged pitch because the source is stationary
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
According to the Doppler effect for a stationary source and an observer moving away from the source:
$$f' = f \left(\frac{v - v_o}{v}\right)$$
Because $v - v_o < v$, the observed frequency $f'$ is strictly less than the emitted source frequency $f$ ($f' < f$). A lower frequency corresponds acoustically to a lower perceived pitch because the observer encounters wave crests at longer time intervals.

options: Higher pitch because waves arrive more frequently
Lower pitch because the relative speed of sound waves is reduced
Unchanged pitch because the source is stationary

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: The escape velocity from the surface of Earth ($M = 6.0 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}$, $R = 6.4 \times 10^6\text{ m}$) is given by $v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$. Its numerical value is approximately
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
The escape velocity $v_{\text{esc}}$ from Earth's surface is calculated as:
$$v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{2 g R} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8\text{ m/s}^2 \times 6.4 \times 10^6\text{ m}} = \sqrt{1.2544 \times 10^8} \approx 1.12 \times 10^4\text{ m/s} = 11.2\text{ km/s}$$
This is the minimum initial ballistic speed required for an unpowered projectile to overcome Earth's gravitational binding energy and reach infinity.

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: A projectile is fired horizontally with a speed of $30\text{ m/s}$ from the top of a cliff of height $45\text{ m}$. Neglecting air resistance and taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, how far from the base of the cliff does the projectile strike the ground?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
For horizontal projectile motion ($u_x = 30\text{ m/s}, u_y = 0$):
1. Time of flight $t$ is determined solely by vertical free-fall:
$$h = \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \implies 45 = \frac{1}{2}(10) t^2 \implies 5t^2 = 45 \implies t^2 = 9 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$
2. Horizontal range $R$:
$$R = u_x t = 30\text{ m/s} \times 3\text{ s} = 90\text{ m}$$.

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding an elastic collision between two i so lated bodies?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_c: Both linear momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
exam-entrance-2016-phys.option_d: Neither momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved.
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation: In classical mechanics, in any i so lated system free from external net forces, total linear momentum is ALWAYS conserved across all collisions (elastic, inelastic, and completely inelastic). An elastic collision is uniquely defined by the additional condition that total kinetic energy is also completely conserved (no mechanical energy is converted into internal thermal heat, sound, or permanent plastic deformation).

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: A circular loop of wire of radius $r = 0.1\text{ m}$ is placed in a uniform magnetic field $B = 0.5\text{ T}$ oriented perpendicular to the plane of the loop. If the magnetic field collapses uniformly to zero in $0.05\text{ seconds}$, what is the magnitude of the average emf induced in the loop?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
Initial magnetic flux through the loop is:
$$\Phi_i = B A = B (\pi r^2) = (0.5\text{ T}) \times \pi \times (0.1\text{ m})^2 = 0.5 \times 0.01 \pi = 0.005\pi\text{ Wb}$$
Final magnetic flux is $\Phi_f = 0$. By Far a day's Law, the induced emf magnitude is:
$$|\mathcal{E}| = \frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t} = \frac{0.005\pi\text{ Wb}}{0.05\text{ s}} = 0.1\pi\text{ V} \approx 0.1 \times 3.1416 = 0.314\text{ V}$$.

If the magnetic field collapses uniformly to zero in $0.05\text{ seconds}$, what is the magnitude of the average emf induced in the loop?

exam-entrance-2016-phys.question_text: What is the binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus that has a total binding energy of $120\text{ MeV}$ and a mass number of $A = 15$?
exam-entrance-2016-phys.explanation:
Binding energy per nucleon ($BE/A$) is the ratio of the total nuclear binding energy to the mass number $A$ (total count of protons and neutrons in the nucleus):
$$\frac{BE}{A} = \frac{120\text{ MeV}}{15\text{ nucleons}} = 8.0\text{ MeV/nucleon}$$
This quantity is the direct physical indicator of nuclear stability.
exam-entrance-2016-phys.text: What is the binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus that has a total binding energy of $120\text{ MeV}$ and a mass number of $A = 15$?

exam-entrance-2016-sat.reading_passage: Sustainable agroforestry and water shed rehabilitation have become central pillars of environmental and rural economic policy in the Ethiopian highlands. Over decades of intensive cereal cultivation and seasonal grazing, steep terrain across regions such as Amhara, Oromia, and Tigray suffered severe top soil erosion, nutrient depletion, and irregular stream hydrology. In response, integrated soil and water conservation (SWC) programs—incorporating deep stone bunding, terracing, and the reintroduction of indigenous leguminous tree species like Acacia albida (Faidherbia albida)—have yielded measurable ecological rest or ation. Faidherbia albida exhibits 'reverse phenology': it sheds its foliage during the wet agricultural season, there by preventing canopy shading over staple crops like teff, maize, and sorghum, while its nitrogen-rich leaf litter enriches top soil organic matter. Concurrently, micro-watershed enclosure systems have curtailed surface rain water run off, allowing ground water aquifers to recharge and perennial natural springs to re-emerge downstream. Economic assessments indicate that smallholder house holds participating in collaborative water shed management experience increased crop yields, reduced seasonal drought vulnerability, and diversified income streams through apiculture and fodder production.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.reading_passage: The rapid expansion of mobile telecommunications and digital payment systems has catalyzed transform ative financial inclusion across Ethiopia. Historically, formal commercial banking services remained heavily concentrated in major urban centers, leaving rural farming communities and micro-merchants under served due to prohibitive physical branch infrastructure costs and strict collateral requirements. The national roll out of mobile money platforms—most not a bly Telebirr alongside licensed private payment system operators—has fundamentally altered this paradigm. By leveraging ubiquitous cellular networks and USSD technology, digital wallets enable users to execute peer-to-peer remittances, purchase utility services, receive agricultural input subsidies, and settle local commerce transactions without a conventional bank account. Financial economists note that real-time mobile liquidity shortens transaction settlement cycles, mitigates the physical theft risks associated with carrying paper cash across rural weekly markets, and builds digital transactional foot prints that enable micro-credit scoring. However, realizing the full potential of this fintech revolution requires overcoming pers is tent rural network connectivity dead zones, expanding digital financial literacy among elderly and rural populations, and maintaining stringent cybersecurity against mobile fraud and phishing vectors.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Since ∠C = 90° and △ABC is isosceles, AC = BC = 4 cm. The hypotenuse AB is: AB = √(AC² + BC²) = √(4² + 4²) = √32 = 4√2 cm.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: Which one of the following can NOT be the degree measure of each interior angle of a regular polygon?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Interior angle of a regular polygon is given by θ = (n - 2) × 180° / n => Exterior angle E = 180° - θ = 360° / n.
• For 140°: E = 40° => n = 360/40 = 9 (regular nonagon)
• For 120°: E = 60° => n = 360/60 = 6 (regular hexagon)
• For 135°: E = 45° => n = 360/45 = 8 (regular octagon)
• For 105°: E = 75° => n = 360/75 = 4.8 (not an integer!). Thus, 105° cannot be an interior angle.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.section_instruction: Solve the mathematical problem and select the correct alternative.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: If f (x) = 10^(2x - 1), then which one of the following is equal to f⁻¹(x)?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Set y = 10^(2x - 1). Take log₁₀ of both sides: log₁₀ y = 2x - 1 => 2x = log y + 1 => x = (1/2) log y + 1/2 = log √y + 1/2. Swap variables: f⁻¹(x) = log √x + 1/2.

Which one of the following is the value of x in the sequence:
23, 34, 56, 89, x, 188, ...?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Examine differences between consecutive terms:
34 - 23 = 11
56 - 34 = 22
89 - 56 = 33
The differences increase by multiples of 11 (11, 22, 33, 44, 55, ...). Next difference should be 44: x = 89 + 44 = 133. Check next term: 133 + 55 = 188 (Matches!).

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: How many numbers in the set {-8, -5, -3, -1, 0, 2, 5, 7, 8} satisfy the condition |5 - 3x| < 11?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Solve inequality: -11 < 5 - 3x < 11. Subtract 5: -16 < -3x < 6. Divide by -3 (flip inequality direction): -2 < x < 16/3 ≈ 5.33. Check set values in range (-2, 5.33):
• -8 (No)
• -5 (No)
• -3 (No)
• -1 (Yes: -2 < -1 < 5.33)
• 0 (Yes)
• 2 (Yes)
• 5 (Yes: 5 < 5.33)
• 7 (No)
• 8 (No) Valid elements: {-1, 0, 2, 5} => Total = 4 numbers.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.section_instruction: Solve the mathematical problem and select the correct alternative.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: A father is 32 years old and his son is 8 years old now. In how many years will the father be three times as old as his son?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Let t be the number of years.
32 + t = 3 (8 + t) => 32 + t = 24 + 3t => 2t = 8 => t = 4.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: A merchant marks up the whole sale cost of an electronic device by 25% to determine the list price. During a seasonal promotion, the merchant offers a 10% discount on the list price. What is the merchant's net profit percentage on the original whole sale cost?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Let the whole sale cost be 100 ETB. Marked price = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125 ETB. Discount of 10% on 125 ETB = 0.10 × 125 = 12.50 ETB. Selling price = 125 - 12.50 = 112.50 ETB. Net profit = 112.50 - 100 = 12.50 ETB on a 100 ETB cost, which is exactly 12.5%.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: A passenger train traveling at a constant speed of 72 km/h completely crosses a bridge of length 180 meters in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Convert speed to meters per second: 72 km/h = 72 × (1000 m / 3600 s) = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s. Total distance covered while crossing the bridge = Speed × Time = 20 m/s × 15 s = 300 meters. Total distance = Length of train (L) + Length of bridge = L + 180 m = 300 m. L = 300 - 180 = 120 meters.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: If 12 skilled laborers can pave a road section in 18 days working 8 hours per day, how many days will 16 laborers take to pave the same road section working 9 hours per day?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Using the work proportionality formula: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂. Total man-hours = 12 × 18 × 8 = 1728 man-hours. For the second team: 16 laborers × D₂ days × 9 hours/day = 144 × D₂ man-hours. Equating work: 144 × D₂ = 1728 => D₂ = 1728 / 144 = 12 days.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: In a class of 50 students, 30 students are registered in the Mathematics Club, 25 are in the Science Club, and 12 are registered in both clubs. How many students are not registered in either club?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
By the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion:
|M ∪ S| = |M| + |S| - |M ∩ S| = 30 + 25 - 12 = 43 students belong to at least one club. Students in neither club = Total students - |M ∪ S| = 50 - 43 = 7 students.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: Two positive integers are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 8 is added to both numbers, the resulting ratio becomes 2 : 3. What is the sum of the two original integers?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Let the two integers be 3k and 5k.
(3k + 8) / (5k + 8) = 2 / 3. Cross-multiplying: 3 (3k + 8) = 2 (5k + 8) 9k + 24 = 10k + 16
10k - 9k = 24 - 16 => k = 8. The original integers are 3 (8) = 24 and 5 (8) = 40. Their sum = 24 + 40 = 64.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: An urn contains 5 red, 4 green, and 3 blue identical balls. If two balls are drawn at random one after another without replacement, what is the probability that both drawn balls are green?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Total balls = 5 + 4 + 3 = 12 balls. Probability the first ball is green = 4 / 12 = 1 / 3. After removing one green ball, 3 green balls remain out of 11 total balls. Probability the second ball is green = 3 / 11. Combined probability = (4/12) × (3/11) = 12 / 132 = 1 / 11.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: A principal sum of 10,000 ETB is deposited into a savings account that yields an annual interest rate of 12% compounded annually. What is the total compound interest earned at the end of 2 years?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Amount A = P (1 + r)^t = 10,000 × (1 + 0.12)² = 10,000 × (1.12)² = 10,000 × 1.2544 = 12,544 ETB. Compound Interest = Total Amount - Principal = 12,544 - 10,000 = 2,544 ETB.
(Note: Simple interest would be 2,400 ETB; compound interest adds the interest on the first year's interest).

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: A logistics transport vehicle drives from Addis Ababa to Adama at an average speed of 60 km/h, and returns along the exact same high way route at an average speed of 40 km/h. What is the average speed of the vehicle for the entire round trip?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
When equal distances (d) are traveled at speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed is the harmonic mean:
Average Speed = (2 × v₁ × v₂) / (v₁ + v₂) = (2 × 60 × 40) / (60 + 40) = 4800 / 100 = 48 km/h.
(A common pitfall is taking the arithmetic mean (60+40)/2 = 50 km/h, which is incorrect because more time is spent at the slower speed).

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 25 cm. If the length of one of the perpendicular legs is 15 cm, what is the area of the triangle?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
By the Pythagorean theorem: a² + b² = c².
15² + b² = 25² => 225 + b² = 625 => b² = 400 => b = 20 cm. Area of right triangle = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 15 cm × 20 cm = 150 cm².

Perimeter of square = 4 × side = 4 × 22 = 88 meters. Circumference of circle = 2πr = 88 meters.
2 × (22/7) × r = 88 (44/7) × r = 88 => r = 88 × (7/44) = 2 × 7 = 14 meters.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: The sum of the interior angles of a regular convex polygon is 1440°. How many sides does this polygon have?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
The sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon is given by: S = (n - 2) × 180°.
(n - 2) × 180° = 1440°
n - 2 = 1440 / 180 = 8
n = 8 + 2 = 10 sides (a decagon).

Consider the following statements:
1. All certified software engineers are proficient in algorithmic thinking.
2. Some university professors are certified software engineers. Which of the following conclusions must logically follow?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.option_a: Some university professors are proficient in algorithmic thinking.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.option_b: All university professors are proficient in algorithmic thinking.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.option_c: All proficient algorithmic thinkers are software engineers.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.option_d: No software engineer is a university professor.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Let S = Software Engineers, A = Proficient in algorithmic thinking, P = Professors. Premise 1: S ⊆ A (All S are A). Premise 2: P ∩ S ≠ ∅ (Some P are S). Therefore, the professors who belong to S must also belong to A, meaning P ∩ A ≠ ∅ (Some professors are proficient in algorithmic thinking).
exam-entrance-2016-sat.section_instruction: Read the statements and logical premises, then choose the valid deductive conclusion.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.text:
Consider the following statements:
1. All certified software engineers are proficient in algorithmic thinking.
2. Some university professors are certified software engineers. Which of the following conclusions must logically follow?
options: Some university professors are proficient in algorithmic thinking.
All university professors are proficient in algorithmic thinking.
All proficient algorithmic thinkers are software engineers.
No software engineer is a university professor.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: In a laboratory experiment: Substance X is hotter than Substance Y. Substance Z is cooler than Substance Y. Substance W is hotter than Substance X. Which substance has the lowest temperature?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Transitive inequality order from hot test to coolest:
W > X (W is hotter than X) X > Y (X is hotter than Y) Y > Z (Z is cooler than Y => Y > Z) Ordering: W > X > Y > Z. Therefore, Substance Z has the lowest temperature.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: Statement: 'If it rains during the harvest week, the cereal crop quality deteriorates.' Which of the following is logically equivalent to this statement?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.option_a: Rain during harvest week always guarantees high cereal crop yields.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.option_b: If it does not rain during the harvest week, the cereal crop quality improves.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.option_c: If the cereal crop quality deteriorates, it must have rained during the harvest week.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.option_d: If the cereal crop quality did not deteriorate, it did not rain during the harvest week.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: A conditional statement (P → Q) is logically equivalent only to its contrapositive (¬Q → ¬P). Here: P = 'It rains during harvest week', Q = 'Cereal crop quality deteriorates'. Contrapositive: ¬Q → ¬P = 'If the cereal crop quality did not deteriorate, then it did not rain during the harvest week'. Option B is the inverse (fallacy) and Option C is the converse (affirming the consequent).
exam-entrance-2016-sat.section_instruction: Evaluate the logic of conditional statements.
exam-entrance-2016-sat.text: Statement: 'If it rains during the harvest week, the cereal crop quality deteriorates.' Which of the following is logically equivalent to this statement?
options: Rain during harvest week always guarantees high cereal crop yields.
If it does not rain during the harvest week, the cereal crop quality improves.
If the cereal crop quality deteriorates, it must have rained during the harvest week.
If the cereal crop quality did not deteriorate, it did not rain during the harvest week.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: Argument: 'Candidate X argues for increasing national investment in solar energy infrastructure. However, Candidate X owns shares in a domestic solar panel manufacturing firm. Therefore, the argument for investing in solar energy is completely invalid.' What logical fallacy is committed in this argument?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: An Ad Hominem Circumstantial fallacy occurs when an opponent's argument is rejected not by refuting the validity or evidence of the argument itself, but by attacking the proponent's personal circumstances, vested interests, or motives. Here, the merits of solar infrastructure investment are ignored.

- Bekele says: 'Gemechu did not take it.'
- Gemechu says: 'Yohannes took it.'
- Yohannes says: 'I did not take it.'
Who is guilty?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Gemechu and Yohannes make contradictory statements ('Yohannes took it ' vs ' Yohannes did not take it'). Exactly one of them is telling the truth and the other is lying. Therefore, Bekele MUST BE LYING. Bekele 's statement ' Gemechu did not take it' is FALSE, which means Gemechu took it. Gemechu is guilty.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: What is the next number in the sequence: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ________?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Method 1: Each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by 2 and adding 1 (a_n = 2 × a_{n-1} + 1):
3 × 2 + 1 = 7
7 × 2 + 1 = 15
15 × 2 + 1 = 31
31 × 2 + 1 = 63
63 × 2 + 1 = 127. Method 2: The differences are powers of 2 (4, 8, 16, 32, 64): 63 + 64 = 127.

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: Determine the next term in the sequence: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, ________?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Examine the successive differences:
6 - 2 = 4
12 - 6 = 6
20 - 12 = 8
30 - 20 = 10
42 - 30 = 12
The differences increase by 2 each step: +4, +6, +8, +10, +12. The next difference is +14. Next term = 42 + 14 = 56.
(Alternatively: n (n + 1) for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 => 7 × 8 = 56).

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: Find the missing term in the pattern: B2D, D4F, F8H, H16J, ________?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation:
Analyze the three components independently:
1. First letter: B (+2) -> D (+2) -> F (+2) -> H (+2) -> J.
2. Numerical middle term: 2 (×2) -> 4 (×2) -> 8 (×2) -> 16 (×2) -> 32.
3. Second letter: D (+2) -> F (+2) -> H (+2) -> J (+2) -> L. Combining all three parts gives: J32L.

To find the med i an, arrange the 9 scores in ascending numerical order:

exam-entrance-2016-sat.question_text: In an agricultural region, grain production increased from 200,000 quintals in Year 1 to 260,000 quintals in Year 2, and reached 312,000 quintals in Year 3. What was the percentage increase in production from Year 2 to Year 3?
exam-entrance-2016-sat.explanation: Production in Year 2 = 260,000 quintals. Production in Year 3 = 312,000 quintals. Absolute increase = 312,000 - 260,000 = 52,000 quintals. Percentage increase = (52,000 / 260,000) × 100% = (52 / 260) × 100% = (1 / 5) × 100% = 20%.

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: How many new hybrid orbitals are formed in the hybridization of the central phosphorus atom in PCl₃?

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: A neutral molecule having the formula AX₂ has two lone pairs on the central atom. What is the hybridization of A?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: Steric number = 2 bonding + 2 lone pairs = 4 domains, which requires sp³ hybridization (bent shape).

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: Which of the following molecules is an AX₃ type with trigonal planar shape?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: In COCl₂, Carbon is bonded to 3 atoms (1 oxygen + 2 chlorines) with 0 lone pairs, giving AX₃ trigonal planar geometry.

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: All molecules with AX₂E₃ type have a linear geometry. Which one of the following fulfills this condition?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: The triiodide ion (I₃⁻) has 2 bonded atoms and 3 lone pairs in equatorial positions (AX₂E₃), giving a linear molecular shape.

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: The type of hybridization in alkanes, alkenes and alkynes respectively are:
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: Carbon atoms in alkanes are sp³ (tetrahedral), in alkenes are sp² (trigonal planar), and in alkynes are sp (linear).

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following diatomic molecules cannot exist (bond order = 0)?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: Beryllium (Be₂) has 4 valence electrons: 2 in σ2s and 2 in σ*2s. Bond order = (2 - 2)/2 = 0, so Be₂ cannot exist.
exam-collection-chem-507.text: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following diatomic molecules cannot exist (bond order = 0)?

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: In the combustion of ethane: CH₃-CH₃ + 7/2 O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O, what hybridization change occurs at the carbon atoms?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: Carbon transitions from sp³ hybridization in ethane (CH₃-CH₃) to sp hybridization in carbon dioxide (O=C=O).
exam-collection-chem-507.text: In the combustion of ethane: CH₃-CH₃ + 7/2 O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O, what hybridization change occurs at the carbon atoms?

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: From CO₂, H₂O, I₃⁻ and BeF₂, which ones share the same linear molecular shape?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: CO₂ (sp, 0 LP), BeF₂ (sp, 0 LP), and I₃⁻ (sp³d, 3 LP equatorial) all possess a linear molecular shape (180°).
exam-collection-chem-507.text: From CO₂, H₂O, I₃⁻ and BeF₂, which ones share the same linear molecular shape?

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a typical property of metals?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: Hardness with brittleness is characteristic of ionic solids and network covalent solids, not metallic crystals (which are ductile and malleable).

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: How many sigma and pi bonds are present in phenol (C₆H₅OH) respectively?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: In phenol: 6 C-C sigma bonds + 5 C-H sigma bonds + 1 C-O sigma bond + 1 O-H sigma bond = 13 sigma bonds; 3 pi bonds in the aromatic benzene ring.
exam-collection-chem-507.text: How many sigma and pi bonds are present in phenol (C₆H₅OH) respectively?

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: How many new hybrid orbitals are formed in the hybridization of the central phosphorus atom in PCl₃?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: Phosphorus in PCl₃ undergoes sp³ hybridization (1 s + 3 p orbitals), forming exactly 4 equivalent sp³ hybrid orbitals (3 bonding, 1 lone pair).
exam-collection-chem-507.text: How many new hybrid orbitals are formed in the hybridization of the central phosphorus atom in PCl₃?

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: What are the overlapping orbitals in the formation of the carbon-carbon sigma bond in ethene (CH₂=CH₂)?
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: Both carbon atoms in ethene are sp² hybridized; their end-to-end overlap forms an sp²-sp² C-C sigma bond.
exam-collection-chem-507.text: What are the overlapping orbitals in the formation of the carbon-carbon sigma bond in ethene (CH₂=CH₂)?

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: The bond order and magnetic nature of the cyanide ion (CN⁻) are:
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: CN⁻ has 14 electrons (i so electronic with N₂). Bond order = (10 - 4)/2 = 3.0, and all electrons are paired (diamagnetic).

exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: Mass m = 0.52 g. Moles of Cr = 0.52 / 52 = 0.01 mol. Since Cr³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Cr, moles of electrons = 3 × 0.01 = 0.03 mol. Charge Q = 0.03 × 96500 = 2895 C. Current I = Q / t = 2895 C / 965 s = 3.0 A.

exam-collection-chem-507.question_text: Two electrolytic cells containing Al (NO₃)₃ and CuCl₂ are connected in series. If 27 g of copper is deposited in one cell, how much Al is deposited in the other? (Cu = 63.5 g/mol, Al = 27 g/mol)
exam-collection-chem-507.explanation: In series, same charge Q passes. Moles of electrons = (27 g / 63.5 g/mol) × 2 = 0.850 mol e⁻. Moles of Al = 0.850 / 3 = 0.283 mol. Mass of Al = 0.283 × 27 g/mol = 7.65 g ≈ 7.6 g.

exam-collection-sat-2014-60.question_text: According to the schedule, which of the following could be true?
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.explanation: Dinner is served on Wed, Fri, Sat (so A and C are false). Floors are polished Monday and never consecutive days, so floors cannot be polished Tuesday (B is false). Plants can be watered on non-consecutive open days when floors are not polished, such as Saturday.
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.section_instruction: Read the passage and answer the following question.
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.passage:
XYZ, a specialty restaurant, is open for business every Monday through Saturday but is closed Sundays. Lunch is the only meal served on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays. Dinner is the only meal served on Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays. The restaurant's floors are polished and its plants are watered only on days that XYZ is open for business, according to the following schedule:
• Plants are watered two days each week, but never on consecutive days and never on the same day that floors are polished.
• Floors are polished on Monday and two other days each week, but never on consecutive days and never on the same day that plants are watered.

exam-collection-sat-2014-60.explanation: Since Monday is a floor-polishing day, Tuesday cannot be a floor-polishing day (non-consecutive rule). The second polishing day must be Wednesday or Thursday. If polished Wednesday, the third day can be Friday or Saturday. Thus Wednesday or Friday are valid floor polishing days.

exam-collection-sat-2014-60.question_text: Five children are sitting in a row. S is sitting next to P but not T. K is sitting next to R who is sitting on the extreme left, and T is not sitting next to K. Who are sitting adjacent to S?
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.explanation: R is at the extreme left (Position 1: R). K is next to R (Position 2: K). T is not next to K, so T is at Position 5. S is next to P and not T, which places S at Position 3 and P at Position 4. The row order is R - K - S - P - T. Thus, K and P sit adjacent to S.

exam-collection-sat-2014-60.question_text: The coconut earned the nickname 'ghost' because:
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.explanation: According to paragraph 2, Portuguese explorers named it 'coco' (ghost) because the three dimples and hairy texture reminded them of a ghost's face.
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.section_instruction: Read the passage and answer the following question.
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.passage:
The coconut is an unusual food for many reasons. It is technically a seed, produced by the coconut palm tree, and as such is one of the largest edible seeds produced by any plant. Its unusual contents also make it unique in the seed world: the interior consists of both 'meat' and 'water.' The meat is the white pith with which we are all familiar, as it is used extensively for cooking and flavourings; the coconut water is a white liquid that is very sweet and thirst-quenching.
Portuguese explorers gave the nut its name in the 15th century, referring to it as coco, meaning 'ghost' in their language. The three dimples and the hairy texture reminded them of a ghost's face, and the tree has retained that name ever since.
The coconut has many varied uses. It is used to make margarine, as well as various cooking oils, and these cooking oils are used by fast-food restaurants around the world to make such diet staples as French fries. The coconut fluid is a favorite drink in hot climates, providing a cool and refreshing beverage right off the tree. This water is also used by manufacturers of various sports drinks because of its isotonic electrolyte properties. Even the shell itself has many uses, including cattle food and fertilizer.

exam-collection-sat-2014-60.option_b: It gets stuck in their intest ines.
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.option_c: Chocolate is made from processed cocoa.
options: It gets stuck in their intest ines.
Chocolate is made from processed cocoa.
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.explanation: The passage explicitly notes that human bodies can process theobromine safely, but dogs and cats cannot metabolize it, making it toxic.
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.section_instruction: Read the passage and answer the following question.
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.passage: Dogs and cats should never be permitted to eat chocolate because chocolate works like a poison in their bodies. Chocolate contains a chemical called theobromine, which is similar to caffeine. Human bodies are able to process the theobromine without any ill side effects, but dogs and cats cannot. Different types of chocolate contain different amounts of theobromine. It would take 20 ounces of milk chocolate to kill a 20-pound dog, but only two ounces of baker's chocolate or six ounces of semi-sweet chocolate. The amounts, of course, are much smaller for a cat, whose body weight is typically less than that of a dog. Most cats are not naturally attracted to eating chocolate, but many dogs are. Dogs by nature will sample nearly anything that they see their masters eating, so pet owners must take care to keep all chocolate products well out of reach of their dogs and cats.

exam-collection-sat-2014-60.question_text: 28 male lions and 172 female lions live in a park. If 35 more male lions are introduced, how many more female lions (x) should be introduced so that 6/7 of the total lions are female?
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.explanation: New male lions = 28 + 35 = 63. Since 6/7 of the total lions are female, 1/7 are male. If 1/7 of total = 63, Total = 63 × 7 = 441. Females needed = (6/7) × 441 = 378. Additional females = 378 - 172 = 206.

exam-collection-sat-2014-60.question_text: What is the value of x in the sequence: 1, 5, 14, 30, x, 91, ...?
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.explanation: The differences are consecutive perfect squares: 5 - 1 = 4 (2²); 14 - 5 = 9 (3²); 30 - 14 = 16 (4²); x - 30 = 25 (5²) → x = 55; 91 - 55 = 36 (6²). Thus x = 55.

exam-collection-sat-2014-60.question_text: In which quadrant is the solution to the system of equations 2x + 3y = 2 and 3x + 2y = 2 located?
exam-collection-sat-2014-60.explanation: Adding both equations: 5x + 5y = 4 → x + y = 4/5. Subtracting: -x + y = 0 → x = y. Thus 2x = 4/5 → x = 2/5, y = 2/5. Since both x > 0 and y > 0, the point (0.4, 0.4) lies in Quadrant I.

exam-collection-econ-480.question_text: What is the primary focus of Aggregate Demand (AD)?
exam-collection-econ-480.option_a: The total out put of goods and services in an economy
exam-collection-econ-480.option_b: The total demand for goods and services at various price levels in an economy
exam-collection-econ-480.option_c: The supply of money in an economy
exam-collection-econ-480.option_d: The total employment in an economy
options: The total out put of goods and services in an economy
The total demand for goods and services at various price levels in an economy
The supply of money in an economy
The total employment in an economy
exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: Aggregate Demand (AD) represents the total quantity of goods and services demanded across all sectors of an economy at a given price level.

exam-collection-econ-480.question_text: Which component is NOT directly a component of Aggregate Demand (AD = C + I + G + (X - M))?
exam-collection-econ-480.option_a: Consumer spending (C)
exam-collection-econ-480.option_b: Investment spending (I)
exam-collection-econ-480.option_c: Government spending (G)
exam-collection-econ-480.option_d: Tax revenues (T)
exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: The components of Aggregate Demand are Consumption (C), Investment (I), Government Purchases (G), and Net Exports (X - M). Tax revenues affect disposable income but are not an expenditure component of AD.

exam-collection-econ-480.question_text: What shape does the short-run Aggregate Supply (SRAS) curve typically have?
exam-collection-econ-480.option_a: Downward sloping
exam-collection-econ-480.option_b: Horizontal
exam-collection-econ-480.option_c: Upward sloping
exam-collection-econ-480.option_d: Vertical
exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: In the short run, higher price levels incentivize producers to increase out put as input costs (wages) are sticky, making SRAS upward sloping.

exam-collection-econ-480.question_text: In the long run, the Aggregate Supply (LRAS) curve is:
exam-collection-econ-480.option_a: Horizontal
exam-collection-econ-480.option_b: Upward sloping
exam-collection-econ-480.option_c: Vertical at the potential out put level
exam-collection-econ-480.option_d: Downward sloping
options: Vertical at the potential out put level
exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: In the long run, prices and wages are fully flexible; the economy produces at full employment/potential GDP, making LRAS vertical.

exam-collection-econ-480.question_text: What can cause a rightward shift in the Aggregate Demand curve?
exam-collection-econ-480.option_a: Increase in consumer confidence and spending
exam-collection-econ-480.option_b: Increase in interest rates
exam-collection-econ-480.option_c: Increase in income taxes
exam-collection-econ-480.option_d: Decrease in government spending
options: Increase in consumer confidence and spending
exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: Increased consumer confidence encourages consumption and investment, shifting Aggregate Demand to the right.

When Aggregate Demand is less than Aggregate Supply

exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: Equilibrium occurs at the price level and real GDP where the aggregate quantity of goods demanded equals the aggregate quantity supplied.

exam-collection-econ-480.question_text: What is a market failure?
exam-collection-econ-480.option_a: A situation where markets allocate resources efficiently
exam-collection-econ-480.option_b: A situation where markets fail to allocate resources efficiently, resulting in welfare loss
exam-collection-econ-480.option_c: A successful market transaction
exam-collection-econ-480.option_d: A government intervention in markets
options: A situation where markets allocate resources efficiently
A situation where markets fail to allocate resources efficiently, resulting in welfare loss
exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: Market failure occurs when the unregulated price mechanism fails to achieve an optimal or socially efficient allocation of resources.

exam-collection-econ-480.question_text: What is a public good?
exam-collection-econ-480.option_a: A good that is excludable and rivalrous
exam-collection-econ-480.option_b: A good that is non-excludable and non-rivalrous in consumption
exam-collection-econ-480.option_c: A good produced by private firms only
exam-collection-econ-480.option_d: A good consumed only by individuals
options: A good that is excludable and rivalrous
A good that is non-excludable and non-rivalrous in consumption
A good produced by private firms only
A good consumed only by individuals
exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: Public goods (e.g. street lighting, national defense) are non-excludable (non-payers cannot be excluded) and non-rival (one person's use does not diminish availability for others).

exam-collection-econ-480.explanation: External i ties occur when producing or consuming a good causes spill over effects on third parties (e.g., pollution as a negative externality).

exam-collection-hist-701.option_a: Abba Gorgorios

exam-collection-hist-701.question_text: History Item 6: In the study of ancient civilizations, what was the primary socioeconomic found ation enabling early urban state formation in river valleys?
exam-collection-hist-701.option_a: Agricultural surplus and irrigation management
exam-collection-hist-701.explanation: Large-scale agriculture in fertile river valleys (Nile, Tigris-Euphrates, Indus, Yellow River) produced the food surpluses required to support non-farming specialized classes and centralized state bureaucracies.

exam-collection-hist-701.question_text: Which species of the genus Homo made the earliest stone tools, consisting of simple flakes and cores known as Oldowan technology?
exam-collection-hist-701.option_a: Homo erectus
exam-collection-hist-701.explanation: Homo habilis ('handy man'), appearing around 2.4 million years ago in East Africa (e.g. Olduvai Gorge, Omo Valley), is credited with crafting Oldowan pebble tools.

exam-collection-hist-701.explanation: Pan-Africanism, championed by figures like W. E. B. Du Bois, Marcus Garvey, and Kwame Nkrumah, advocated solidarity, political independence, and unity among all African peoples.
